name: ScrapingBee
summary: ScrapingBee is a hosted API you call with a URL, and it returns the page's HTML or extracted data, handling proxies and JavaScript rendering for you.

free_plan_covers.note: New accounts get 1,000 free API credits as a one-time trial with no credit card required, not an ongoing monthly free plan; the pricing page's own plans all start at $19/month.

first_paid_usd_month.note: Hobby plan is $19/month for 75,000 API credits.

portability.note: It's a proprietary REST API with its own credit system, though sending a URL and getting back HTML is a common enough shape that switching providers mainly means changing the request code.

scraper_runs.note: You call their API with a target URL and parameters, and ScrapingBee's servers fetch the page and return it.

js_rendering.note: A plain request costs 1 credit, turning on JavaScript rendering (the default) costs 5 credits, and adding a premium or stealth proxy on top can cost up to 75 credits.

ai_ready_output.note: Its ai_query and ai_extract_rules parameters use AI to return structured data straight from a page instead of raw HTML you'd have to parse yourself.

price_per_1k_pages.value: About $0.25 per 1,000 pages without JavaScript rendering, or about $1.27 per 1,000 pages with it turned on, on Hobby ($19/month for 75,000 credits: 1 credit per plain page, 5 credits per JS-rendered page).
price_per_1k_pages.note: Math from the Hobby plan's price and credit allowance, applied to ScrapingBee's published per-request credit costs.

setup.step: Create a free ScrapingBee account and copy your API key from the dashboard.
Install the SDK with npm install scrapingbee.
Add your key as SCRAPINGBEE_API_KEY in your environment file.
In a server route, create a ScrapingBeeClient with your key and call client.get({ url, params }) to fetch a page.

builder_notes: Keep SCRAPINGBEE_API_KEY server-side and call the API from a route handler or server action, never from client code.
Only turn on JavaScript rendering or premium/stealth proxies when a page actually needs them, since each one multiplies the credit cost.
Respect each target site's robots.txt and terms of service before scraping it.
